matches.match_basis: DOI, full title, five ordered authors, year and original-specific empirical fingerprints agree.

all_shipped_match_analysis.alias_analysis: Exact original DOI is printed in Archer 2015 and the deposited current reference array; baseline title/authors/year match. No identifier alias is needed to establish representation.
all_shipped_match_analysis.alternate_report_analysis: Archer 2015 reports the 2014 national sample of 3,658. DeWitt 2016 explicitly reuses that national sample and index, but also analyses a distinct 2014-15 targeted sample of 6,861 from 18 schools. For the reused national sample, distribution and demographic results are repeat reporting, not a second independent dataset. However, DeWitt 2016 independently reports the same low/high distribution and South Asian/high-cultural-capital/top-set pattern in its targeted sample as well. Current Results explicitly attributes the younger-cohort distribution to BOTH papers, and Discussion explicitly places BOTH in the retested set. Its new 7,013-person survey measures the corresponding distribution and demographic pattern. Therefore the 2016 report is an empirically tested original paper, not merely the source of an instrument or an alternate title/version of the 2015 article. No claim is made that every 2016 analysis is retested.

decisions.rationale: Author 2 et al. (2015) binds to Archer, Dawson, DeWitt, Seakins and Wong: the current paper repeats the 14-item index, national younger-sample gender composition, 27.2% low/67.6% medium distribution, demographic/setting patterns, and especially the distinctive 37% versus 9% high/low-science-capital A-level aspiration comparison printed in Archer 2015 Table 2. The complete deposited bibliography identifies this paper, while its other Archer 2015 entry is the Black-students/parents paper, not this index-and-national-survey report. This is joint bibliography plus original-specific empirical fingerprint evidence, not a year match. The sole shipped counterpart is this exact original; exporting target 0 again would duplicate row 5.
decisions.strongest_contrary_evidence: Previously an anonymized 2015 self-citation could not be equated with shipped Archer 2015. This remains valid history, but the new bibliography and exact original empirical fingerprints now close that identity gap.

actual_empirical_retest.original_finding: Younger students’ science capital is unevenly distributed/patterned by demographic characteristics and science set, and higher capital relates to A-level/university science aspirations.
actual_empirical_retest.current_corresponding_analysis: New age-17/18 survey distribution, gender/ethnicity/cultural-capital/set comparisons, A-level course enrolment and post-18 university intentions.

Bibliography and full frontmatter identify two journal reports with different author lists and titles. Distinctness is additionally grounded in the 2016 report’s 6,861-person targeted sample and new analyses, not DOI/year difference. No supplied alias maps DeWitt 2016 to row 5.

all_shipped_match_analysis.closest_chain_analysis: The current paper directly attributes tested younger-cohort findings to both papers. DeWitt 2016 is not an intervening report that removes the directly named Archer 2015 aspiration finding; Archer 2015 is not merely an ancestor for that separately attributed current comparison. Conversely, re-reporting the national sample does not exhaust DeWitt 2016 because its targeted-sample distribution/pattern is also inside the directly attributed retested set. Count original papers with an actually retested finding, not independent tests or every dataset.

decisions.rationale: Archer 2015 reports the 2014 national sample of 3,658. DeWitt 2016 explicitly reuses that national sample and index, but also analyses a distinct 2014-15 targeted sample of 6,861 from 18 schools. For the reused national sample, distribution and demographic results are repeat reporting, not a second independent dataset. However, DeWitt 2016 independently reports the same low/high distribution and South Asian/high-cultural-capital/top-set pattern in its targeted sample as well. Current Results explicitly attributes the younger-cohort distribution to BOTH papers, and Discussion explicitly places BOTH in the retested set. Its new 7,013-person survey measures the corresponding distribution and demographic pattern. Therefore the 2016 report is an empirically tested original paper, not merely the source of an instrument or an alternate title/version of the 2015 article. No claim is made that every 2016 analysis is retested. All supplied shipped counterparts and the root baseline have been checked: none represents this report.
decisions.strongest_contrary_evidence: The strongest objection is that the numerical historical comparator actually used in the current distribution analysis (27.2% low, 67.6% medium, and mean 41.57 after rescaling 43.65/105 to 100) is the 2014 national sample already in Archer 2015 and reprinted in DeWitt 2016. The current paper does not separately tabulate a contrast with the targeted 2014-15 sample, and it does not repeat DeWitt 2016’s distinctive science-versus-cultural-capital prediction models or item-importance regressions; related hierarchical regressions are explicitly planned for future work. Thus the two journal publications and grouped Discussion citation alone would be insufficient. The additional original-specific evidence is DeWitt 2016’s independently reported targeted-sample distribution/demographic finding, which is inside the current paper’s explicitly attributed set-wide retest of younger cohorts. The lack of a separate targeted-sample statistical contrast does not cancel that conceptual empirical retest under Rule 2.

actual_empirical_retest.original_finding: In both the reused 2014 national survey and the distinct 2014-15 targeted survey, only a small minority have high science capital and it is concentrated among South Asian/Middle Eastern students, students with higher cultural capital, and top science sets. The targeted sample independently shows the low/high distribution and demographic pattern.
actual_empirical_retest.current_corresponding_analysis: The new age-17/18 survey’s low/medium/high distribution and ethnic/cultural-capital/science-set analyses retest those younger-cohort patterns; current Results expressly attributes the distribution to Author 2 2015 and Author 3 2016, and Discussion expressly places both in the retested set.
actual_empirical_retest.tested_finding_limits: No retest is inferred for the 2016 paper’s item-level beta rankings, its science-versus-cultural-capital predictive superiority, zoo-visitation coefficient or qualitative pen portraits. Merely using its instrument would not qualify.
